entities.text: Suo Motu Public Interest Litigation No.3 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The applicant- bakeries are seeking setting aside/withdrawal of the notice dated 29 th January 2025 issued by the Medical Officer of Health, E Ward, Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai.
An alternative prayer has been made for a direction upon the respondent-Authority not to enforce the notice dated 29th January 2025.

The applicant-bakeries have also made a prayer for extension of the time by one year for transition of the bakeries from conventional fuel to cleaner fuel regime so as to comply the directions issued by the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai vide its notice dated 29th January 2025.
2. Twelve bakeries have approached the Court through this Interim Application.
The applicant-bakeries state that there are about 750 bakeries in the City of Mumbai and about 2000 bakeries in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region.
These bakeries have long and rich cultural history dating back beyond a century and these are largely family-run business.

They have given a description of the produces from their bakeries and stated that these products are the only source of food to the citizens and their business provides dignified employment to thousands of unskilled and semi-skilled laborers.
In this Interim Application, the applicant-bakeries have referred to the notices issued to them whereby they have been intimated the timeline for switching over to gas/electrical fuel source.
In connection therewith, B.D.Pandit-SPS 3 913- IA-9522-25 bakeries.doc
they have also referred to the Circular dated 22 nd November 2024.

sentences.text: The applicants have further stated that the implication of the order dated 9th January 2025 would have a far reaching effect and would cause hardship to the public at large.
3. An affidavit dated 21st August 2025 sworn on behalf of the Applicant No.9 (Indian Bakery) has been tendered in the Court.

In this affidavit, the Applicant No. 9 states as under :-
5.
The wood-fired oven in my bakery occupies an area of approximately 180 sq. ft. (12 ft x 15 ft).
While my bakery operates only one oven, most bakeries operate two such ovens, made of brick and stone and permanently embedded into the structure
Transitioning to PNG ovens requires complete demolition of these wood-fired ovens and installation of new PNG-compatible structures.
This is a complex and time-consuming process and will entail a shutdown of the oven while this is underway.

Based on industry quotations and consultations, this change will take at least two months and cost between Rs 15-20 lakhs, including demolition, civil work,
equipment purchase, safety upgrades, and gas fitting.

These are major changes,
which can only be commenced once there is assurance of a reliable PNG supply.
An abrupt shutdown of bakeries without workable alternatives will disrupt supply chains, affect consumers, and cause unnecessary hardship to the poor.
This includes persons engaged in and dependent on the trade and/or persons who depend on pav as an affordable food item.
6. I have set out in paragraph 10 below, why LPG as a fuel is not feasible, practical, viable or safe.
The authorities concerned have recognised this and have therefore themselves contemplated a switch to PNG.
7. All the Applicants herein have already made applications to Mahanagar Gas Limited ("MGL"), the only authorised PNG distributor for new connections.
Upon inquiries about the status of our applications, we have been informed that PNG pipelines have to be laid onto the roads, for connectivity and supply to our area.

This will probably be available by mid - 2026, subject to permission from the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai ("MCGM") to undertake B.D.Pandit-SPS 4 913- IA-9522-25 bakeries.doc road digging and laying of pipelines.
MGL has also orally clarified that this process can only commence after the monsoon season, creating further unavoidable delays.
In these circumstances, initiating reconstruction of ovens without certainty of supply would be counterproductive, economically burdensome, and leave the bakery inoperable.
8. The use of PNG ovens also requires upgrading the sanctioned electricity load.

Even though electricity is not needed as a heat generator, PNG ovens are more complex than wood fired ovens,
since gas is capable of rapid disposal and requires several additional features such as an ignition system, safety cut-off valves, exhaust and temperature control system.
These safety and automation systems operate on electricity and consume a higher load than wood-fired ovens.

sentences.text: of electricity load involves applications, assessments, and infrastructure changes through the local electricity distribution company, which further adds to the timeline and complexity.
9. Electric ovens are not a viable alternative due to their high operational costs.
The capital cost of setting up a comparable electrically operated oven would be significantly higher than that of a PNG oven.
To the best of my knowledge, no bakery of comparable size and scale in Mumbai currently uses electricity as a primary fuel source for baking."

4. In his affidavit, Applicant No.9 states that he is committed to transition of PNG Ovens as soon as supply of PNG becomes available and undertakes to fully cooperate with the Authorities for inspection and compliance requirements.

5. Mr. Venkatesh Dhond, the learned senior counsel for the applicant- bakeries submits that the applicant-bakeries were not made parties and not heard before the order dated 9th January 2025 came to be passed.

It is submitted that the applicant-bakeries are required to demolish existing buildings and invest huge money for shifting to alternative fuel source and it would take some time to switch over to clean fuel source.

The learned senior counsel submits that much before the order dated 9 th January 2025 was passed, many of the bakeries had been in correspondence with the Mahanagar Gas Limited (in short, MGL) for providing PNG connections.

The learned senior counsel tendered copies of e-mails in course of the hearing when this matter was taken up after the recess to apprise the Court B.D.Pandit-SPS 5 913- IA-9522-25 bakeries.doc that one Pahelvi Bakery was, in fact, given clearance by the Maharashtra Pollution Control Board and the MGL for PNG supply.

The learned senior counsel has also taken us through the correspondences by the Joint Committee of India Bakers Association and a proposal from the Government for incentive to the Industries which switches over to clean and green energy system.

In sum and substance, this is the stand taken by the applicant-bakeries that they have been making bona-fide endeavors but for a confirm commitment to supply PNG by the MGL and other logistics difficulties they are unable to shift to green fuel regime and, therefore, are constrained to approach this Court seeking extension of time by one year.

6. Mr. Darius Khambata, the learned amicus curiae has taken us through the observations made by this Court in its order dated 9 th January 2025 and submitted that the issue of shifting to the green alternative fuel system by the bakeries was discussed by this Court and, after having noticed the previous notices issued and the adverse environmental impact due to coal and wood burning, a timeline has been set for switching over to the alternative energy source.

The learned amicus curiae referred to paragraph no. 14 and 15 of the said order wherein this Court observed that effective and immediate steps are required to be taken to control air pollution by the hotels and bakeries.

The learned amicus curiae would contend that the applicant-bakeries have no right in law under Article 19(g) of the Constitution of India to carry on business through a polluting establishment and the right of the citizens under Article 21 of the Constitution of India must prevail over the individual rights of the applicant-bakeries even though some hardship is caused to them.
7.

The observations and directions of the Court in paragraph nos. 14 and 15 of the order dated 9th January 2025 are extracted hereunder :-

Insofar as the pollution created by Hotels, Bakeries and Bhattis etc., is concerned,
the same is caused as these units use either wood or coal.
We have been informed by the Municipal Corporation as also B.D.Pandit-SPS 6 913- IA-9522-25 bakeries.doc
the Pollution Control Board

that very recently steps are taken to stop these units from using the traditional fuel and shift to the alternate green fuels like CNG, Gas etc.,
which would curtail the Pollution and Particulate Matter (PM), being emitted by this units.
We have perused the notice issued by the Municipal Corporation which calls upon these units to shift to the alternate green fuels within a period of one year.

Insofar as the Maharashtra Pollution Control Board is concerned, copy of the show cause notice issued to one Yazdani Bakery, Fort, dated 7 January 2025 which is just two days before the present hearing, calling upon the Bakery to show cause as to why it shall not be closed as it is using wood as fuel without obtaining prior consent, is placed on record.

15. In our opinion, urgent and effective measures are required to be taken against such Bakery units so that such units which are in large number in the city, do not generate air pollution and more particularly, limiting hazardous particulate matter.
These units need to take urgent steps to change to the alternate fuels by discarding the use of wood and coal.
In our opinion, it is not a task which would require a long period of one year as being contemplated by the MCGM.
We are of the opinion that within six months from today, the Bakery units need to be directed to stop using wood and coal and by converting these units to use CNG, Gas or Green fuels etc.
Such directions be issued by the concerned authorities like the MPCB and the MCGM.
We may also observe that henceforth no new licenses, approvals and permissions to open bakeries or similar businesses shall be granted permitting the use of coal and wood.

All new licenses be granted for opening Bakeries, Restaurants, Bhattis etc., by incorporating a condition that such units shall use only Green fuel, CNG, Gas etc.,
and not use wood and coal.

It is only on verification of such compliance, final permission be granted to such units".
8.

"P.C.
1. Not on board.
Upon mentioning, taken on production board.

sentences.text: Now, the application has been filed for extension of time.
5. List the application on 28th July 2025.

In the peculiar facts and for the B.D.Pandit-SPS 7 913- IA-9522-25 bakeries.doc reasons mentioned in the application, we are satisfied that time granted by this Court in the interregnum needs to be extended till the next date.
6. Till next date, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation shall not act on the Notice dated 29th January 2025."
9. This Interim Application was filed on 9 th June 2025 and taken on Board upon mentioning on 25 th June, 2025.
It was again listed on 7 th July 2025 and taken up for hearing on 8 th July 2025 when a Coordinate Bench of this Court passed the above order extending the timeline till 28 th July 2025.

But there is no material on record to indicate why the applicant-bakeries did not approach the Court when they got the knowledge of timeline fixed under the Court's order through the notice dated 29 th January 2025, at least for projecting their difficulties in getting PNG supply.

In this Interim Application, except stating that there was a representation made by the Association of Bakers no other detail has been furnished by the applicant- bakeries as to when they made applications for PNG supply and about the follow up steps taken by them.
This is not even indicated in this Interim Application that they made endeavors for installing alternative energy source so as to keep their bakeries running.
Whereas, the order dated 9 th January 2025 records that immediate steps are required to be taken by the polluting establishments.

The affidavit sworn on behalf of the Applicant No. 9, a copy of which has been tendered in the Court, only narrates the difficulties in transforming the bakeries from conventional fuel to green and safer fuel source and merely states that all the applicant-bakeries have made applications for supply of PNG.

We further find that the applicant-bakeries did not take any step after the interim order extending the timeline was passed by the Coordinate Bench on 8th July 2025; that was deadline fixed under the Court's order.
It was only on 20 th August 2025 that this Interim Application was taken on Production Board on the request made by the learned counsel for the applicant-bakeries, after the extended time had lapsed.

The learned counsel appearing for the MGL stated that on site B.D.Pandit-SPS 8 913- IA-9522-25 bakeries.doc inspection it was observed that it is not feasible to provide PNG supply to the applicant-bakeries.

Though the learned senior counsel for the applicant- bakeries took objection on the ground that no such statement has been made on oath, we are not inclined to ask the respondents to file their affidavit-in-opposition to this Interim Application.
In a public interest litigation, the Court is concerned with the larger public interest.
The right of a citizen to have a clean environment has attained the status of fundamental right under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.
This is well remembered that hardship to a few is not a ground to deprive the larger section of the society to have the clean and green environment.

This is nowhere stated in this application that use of conventional fuel would not produce air pollution rather it is an admitted position that there are serious implications of the use of conventional fuel.
The risk of potential harm to human health would definitely tilt the balance in favor of the larger public interest.
It would take precedence over unemployment, business prospects and other factors of similar nature.

To this, we may only observe that the Courts do not pass orders on mere probabilities (refer, " Razia Begum v. Sahebzadi Anwar Begum and Ors." 1958 AIR 886).

sentences.text: In "Razia Begum" , an application under Order I Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure was moved for addition of the intervenors as party-defendants.
The main ground urged on their behalf was that their addition in the pending suit as party-defendants would avoid multiplicity of litigation.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that the suggestion made on behalf of the the intervenors that the suit would lead to multiplicity of proceedings was founded on such assumption that no Court B.D.Pandit-SPS 9 913- IA-9522-25 bakeries.doc of law would assume.
In our opinion, this Interim Application has to be decided on the basis of averments made therein and, at the best, the documents and the affidavit tendered in the Court.

However, this Interim Application and the other documents lack in material particulars and we do not find any justifiable reason also to extend the timeline indicated in the notice dated 29th January 2025 which is based on the order passed by this Court.
11. Interim Application No.9522 of 2025 is accordingly dismissed.

[AARTI SATHE, J.] [SHREE CHANDRASHEKHAR, J.]
